title: What to Think About When You’re
Thinking About a Job Change

takeaways.headline: Interestingness is a weak guide to job satisfaction.
paragraphs: Career quizzes tend to focus on finding jobs that fit your interests, but it's important to consider other (stronger) predictors of satisfaction such as autonomy, connection with colleagues, and whether the work feels meaningful.

takeaways.headline: Diagnose your dissatisfaction before deciding to leave.
paragraphs: Some feelings are likely to follow you from job to job, but others won't. Consider whether reshaping your current role could help.

takeaways.headline: A bigger salary does not guarantee a happier working life.
paragraphs: Higher income is more strongly associated with life satisfaction than with job satisfaction or moment-to-moment happiness, so weigh a raise against your other priorities.

takeaways.headline: Learn what a job feels like before committing to it.
paragraphs: Imagination is often a bad guide, and it is subject to biases. It can be better to ask people doing the work about their typical day, and test potential career changes through small projects, courses, volunteering, or temporary roles.

takeaways.headline: A fading honeymoon period does not mean a job change was a mistake.
paragraphs: Even if you do change job and experience a boost in happiness/satisfaction, that boost is likely to fade with time. That being said, temporary improvements can still make a move worthwhile.
